# Scan-first follow-up

The confirmed teaching failure was Android bitmap ownership. In the installed MediaPipe library, BitmapImageContainer.close calls Bitmap.recycle. LookEmbedder wrapped the caller's bitmap directly. It was destroyed before fingerprinting/JPEG saving and could also destroy the second-reader crop. The previous JVM persistence tests did not exercise this library. LookEmbedder now owns separate, bounded pixels; ReferenceSaver checks the original remains readable through extraction and persistence.

The user's manually entered row also mixed manufacturer and product/ingredient fields: APEX was saved as brand and P-500 as generic. Observed OCR showed P-500 and Paracetamol. The row was not silently rewritten by a diagnostic script. The new Teach > Read label and update details allows a reviewed correction while preserving its ID and prescribed times.

List now opens with Scan a new medicine. Capture the name/composition, then review a filled identity card. OCR supplies an immediate draft; the on-device vision model transcribes a structured draft. Up to three sides can be captured in one enrollment, and eight references may be kept per medicine. Only missing or incorrect fields need correction. Package dosing instructions, mg/kg, daily maxima, dates and batch/storage lines are not identity strengths. The app does not infer ingredients or units from brand names.

Prescribed times are chosen separately using chips or custom entry. They can be added later. Save medicine and photos writes the label and all captured references in one acknowledged transaction. Missing fields and model failures are explicit and do not silently create a complete identity. Manual entry and CSV remain optional fallbacks.

The follow-up creates core/LabelDraft.kt, LabelEvidence.kt and LabelPrompt.kt; data/ReferenceSaver.kt; ui/EnrollmentController.kt and EnrollmentScreen.kt. It updates LookEmbedder, GemmaInputs, GemmaStats, StripParser, Store, TeachingCapture, TeachingCamera, TeachTab, ListTab and English/Hindi CoreLabels. The only Gradle addition selects a native test runner; dependency/tool versions were unchanged.

260 JVM tests pass. Six native checks passed on the connected Android 16 phone: caller bitmap ownership, actual JPEG persistence, reopen/decode, bundled OCR plus local vision on an isolated fixture, and read-only extraction from the user's saved P-500 and Parawel-325 DT photos. P-500 extraction took 4,384 ms and Parawel took 4,724 ms. Tests never wrote fixtures to the normal medicine list. Read device-check-result.txt for the runner outcome.

Actual photographs exposed additional extraction mistakes. OCR now excludes number/unit and pharmacopoeia text from brand candidates, recognizes spaces around product hyphens and normalizes joined brand numbers. A model draft that uses the manufacturer or ingredient as the trade name is reconciled with printed OCR product evidence. Blank optional arrays are normalized; release and variant output are constrained. DT is supported as a printed dispersible variant, including a separate DT line. Dispersible is not kept as part of the ingredient name. Unsupported variants and invalid strengths still fail validation.

Gemma requests now use a single deadline for native conversation setup, generation and JSON fallback. Calls return Busy instead of queuing, and a timed-out native job retains exclusive engine ownership until its cleanup finishes. Native cancellation and close cannot race. The device runner opens the app visibly; the earlier background-only runner stalled on this phone and was terminated rather than counted as a pass.

Read label and update details automatically rereads the most recent saved photo when available. A fresh bounded OCR task and the same local vision extraction fill the review card. Pixels remain owned until processing completes. The family must review the result before Save; earlier user records are never silently overwritten. IDs and prescribed times are preserved.

The phone's store now contains three user-created medicines and three reference photos, which remained after APK updates and were reopened for inspection. The earlier APEX/generic mixup and missing DT need reviewed correction through Read label and update details. Live two/three-strip selection, photo/crop alignment, glare and damaged-print performance still require physical trials. No fake medicine or dose mark was added by testing. No accuracy percentage is claimed from these two photographs.

To reproduce native checks, build :app:assembleDebugAndroidTest, install app-debug-androidTest.apk and run `adb shell am instrument -w app.stripsense.test/app.stripsense.device.CoreDeviceChecks`. The runner stores fixtures only under a temporary cache folder and removes it. User photographs, raw audio and transcripts must not be logged. Label rejection diagnostics contain only the failed field category.

Next on the phone: open Teach > Read label and update details for the existing row, capture real print, review the filled card and save. Inspect reference count, restart and inspect the photo again. Then scan two/three separated strips and exercise wrong-strength and partial-print cases without marking any real dose unless explicitly confirmed. Keep full-print and conflicting-evidence safeguards intact. No commit or push.
